title: Aaj Tak
description: Indian news channel. Newslaundry reports an Aaj Tak presenter claimed the NGO Hami Nepal received Rs 20 crore from Coca-Cola and Viber.

title: Access Now
description: Digital rights organisation. Statements on the Telegram ban (29 July 2025) and on the September 2025 crackdown and digital repression.

title: Amnesty International
description: International rights organisation. Its report of 8 December 2025 says it verified eyewitness accounts, photographic and video evidence.

title: Annapurna Post
description: Nepali-language daily started in 2002, published by Annapurna Media Network from Corporate Tower, Tinkune, Kathmandu (Wikipedia).

title: Armed Police Force
description: Paramilitary police founded on 24 October 2001 under the Ministry of Home Affairs. Inspector General Raju Aryal until 1 May 2026, then Narayan Dutta Poudel.

title: Australian Embassy in Nepal
description: Australian diplomatic mission. Listed as a signatory of the joint statement of 9 September 2025.

title: Avenues Television
description: Television channel for which video journalist Suresh Rajak was filming from the roof of a building at Tinkune on 28 March 2025.

title: BBC
description: British public broadcaster. Its investigation of the 8 September police shootings, built on more than 4,000 videos and photographs plus police radio logs, was reported on 26 and 27 February 2026.

title: Bhatbhateni Supermarket
description: Retail supermarket chain; Wikipedia's account of the 2025 protests says multiple outlets were damaged.

title: Bibeksheel Sajha Party
description: Party headed by Samiksha Baskota. It announced a merger with the Rastriya Swatantra Party on 30 November 2025.

title: Bir Hospital
description: Hospital in central Kathmandu established in 1889 by Bir Shumsher Jang Bahadur Rana.

title: B. P. Koirala Institute of Health Sciences
description: Autonomous health sciences university and hospital in Dharan, Sunsari, founded 18 January 1993; Wikipedia's account of the protests lists it among the hospitals named.

title: British Embassy Kathmandu
description: UK diplomatic mission. Listed as a signatory of the joint statement of 9 September 2025.

title: Central Investigation Bureau
description: Nepal Police unit that arrested Rabi Lamichhane on 18 October 2024.

title: Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs
description: Its spokesperson congratulated Karki on becoming prime minister of Nepal's interim government (reported 14 September 2025).

title: Civil Aviation Authority of Nepal
description: Operator of Tribhuvan International Airport (Wikipedia).

title: Civil Service Hospital
description: Hospital at Minbhawan, Kathmandu, handed over in 2008 as a 132-bed hospital and inaugurated in 2009.

title: Commission for the Investigation of Abuse of Authority
description: Anti-corruption body. Its central office in Tangal was reported set on fire on 9 September 2025.

title: Committee to Protect Journalists
description: International press-freedom organisation that urged Nepali lawmakers to reject the Social Media Bill (14 Feb 2025) and criticised the September 2025 platform ban.

title: Confederation of Nepalese Industries
description: Industry body. An official was quoted by IANS on the damage reported by major business enterprises.

title: Cooperative savings fraud victims
description: Depositors in fraudulent savings cooperatives who have protested repeatedly in Kathmandu, mostly on the Maitighar-Baneshwar stretch, demanding return of their money. The Kathmandu Post counts more than 2,000 victims filing complaints against 123 cooperatives owing over Rs960 million.

title: CPN (Maoist Centre)
description: Party chaired by Pushpa Kamal Dahal. Dissolved on 4 November 2025 when its central committee merged it with other communist parties into the Nepali Communist Party. Headquarters: Perisdanda, Koteshwor, Kathmandu (Wikipedia).

title: CPN-UML
description: Communist Party of Nepal (Unified Marxist-Leninist). Chaired by KP Sharma Oli since 2014. Won 79 seats in the 2022 election, the second largest party. Wikipedia lists its headquarters at Thapathali, Kathmandu, and reports that protesters vandalised the headquarters in September 2025.

title: CPN (Unified Socialist)
description: Party named by Setopati as the party of former prime minister Jhalanath Khanal when his wife was injured on 9 September 2025.

title: Cyabra
description: Cyber intelligence company based in Tel Aviv, Israel, that analyses online disinformation and fake accounts.

title: Dainik Bhaskar
description: Indian Hindi daily. Alt News says its national editor shared an Indonesian protest video as showing Nepal.

title: Department of Prison Management
description: Government body that gave the prisoner escape and return figures cited in the reporting on the September 2025 jail breaks.

title: Dharan Sub-Metropolitan City
description: Local government of Dharan, eastern Nepal; Harka Sampang was mayor from 23 May 2022 to 19 January 2026 (Wikipedia).

title: Digital Rights Nepal
description: Rights group whose president, Bhola Nath Dhungana, criticised the 4 September 2025 closure as a hit on fundamental rights.

title: Discord
description: Chat platform (Discord Inc., San Francisco, founded May 2015). On the list of 26 blocked platforms; Wikipedia reports it was nevertheless used in the 2025 Nepal protests to coordinate and to help choose a new prime minister.

title: District Administration Office, Kathmandu
description: Office of the Chief District Officer of Kathmandu; it issued the curfew order of 9 September 2025 under CDO Chhabi Rijal (Deccan Herald).

title: District Administration Office, Lalitpur
description: Office of the Chief District Officer of Lalitpur, Suman Ghimire, which applied the 9 September 2025 curfew to parts of wards 2, 4, 9, 18 and 25.

title: Election Commission of Nepal
description: Constitutional body founded 12 November 1951, headquartered at Kantipath, Kathmandu; it recognised Gagan Thapa's leadership of the Nepali Congress on 16 January 2026 (Himal Press).

title: Embassy of Finland in Nepal
description: Finnish diplomatic mission. Listed as a signatory of the joint statement of 9 September 2025.

title: Embassy of France in Nepal
description: French diplomatic mission. Listed as a signatory of the joint statement of 9 September 2025.

title: Embassy of Germany in Nepal
description: German diplomatic mission. Listed as a signatory of the joint statement of 9 September 2025 by Diplomat Nepal only (B360 Nepal lists seven missions without Germany).

title: Embassy of Japan in Nepal
description: Japanese diplomatic mission. Listed as a signatory of the joint statement of 9 September 2025.

title: Embassy of Norway in Nepal
description: Norwegian diplomatic mission. Listed as a signatory of the joint statement of 9 September 2025 by Diplomat Nepal only (B360 Nepal lists seven missions without Norway).

title: Embassy of the Republic of Korea in Nepal
description: South Korean diplomatic mission. Listed as a signatory of the joint statement of 9 September 2025.

title: European Union Delegation to Nepal
description: EU mission in Kathmandu; Ambassador Veronique Lorenzo welcomed Karki's appointment.

title: Everest Hospital
description: Hospital in New Baneshwar named in reporting as having received dead or dying protesters on 8 September 2025.

title: Facebook (Meta Platforms)
description: Facebook is a product of Meta Platforms (founded 4 February 2004, headquartered in Menlo Park, California), which also owns Instagram, WhatsApp and Threads. Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp and Messenger were on the list of 26 platforms blocked in Nepal on 4 September 2025.

title: Federal Parliament of Nepal
description: Bicameral legislature. Both houses met at the International Convention Centre, New Baneshwor, until September 2025, when protesters stormed and burned the building; the lower house now meets in a new Parliament House within the Singha Durbar premises (Wikipedia).

title: Federation of Nepali Journalists
description: Professional journalists' association; its website lists membership of the International Federation of Journalists and IFEX (accessed 2026-10-05).

title: International Federation for Human Rights (FIDH)
description: International human rights federation. Co-signed a statement on 9 September 2025 with OMCT, FORUM-ASIA, CIVICUS and nine Nepali civil society organisations, and the 12-13 September joint statement.

title: Federation of Nepalese Chambers of Commerce and Industry
description: Private-sector federation. Its president gave a preliminary private-sector loss estimate of NPR 80 to 100 billion to Prime Minister Sushila Karki on 21 September 2025.

title: Freedom Forum
description: Nepali NGO working on democracy, human rights, press freedom, freedom of expression and the right to information; its site says it was established in February 2005 by media professionals, legal experts and academics.

title: Gauri Bahadur Karki inquiry commission
description: Commission led by former judge Gauri Bahadur Karki that reported on the Gen Z protests; reporting says it largely stays silent on the second day of violence.

title: GenZ Martyrs' Family Welfare Society
description: Society that organised a programme in New Baneshwor on 8 September 2026, attended by the Home Minister, other ministers and families of the dead.

title: Gen Z movement (Nepal, 2025)
description: Loose network of youth groups, including Hami Nepal, that led the September 2025 protests and sent representatives to the army-mediated talks. Reports show several groups with different preferred interim leaders.

title: Commission investigating the 8-9 September 2025 events (Karki commission)
description: Government-appointed commission chaired by retired Supreme Court judge Gauri Bahadur Karki. It handed its report to Prime Minister Sushila Karki on 8 March 2026 and recommended criminal investigation of Oli, Lekhak and IGP Khapung and action against other officials (Onlinekhabar, 25 March 2026).

title: Gorkha Media Network
description: Media company where Rabi Lamichhane was managing director; a parliamentary committee concluded cooperative funds were funnelled into it. An audit report cited by the Kathmandu Post counts Rs109.936 million deposited into its accounts.

title: Hami Nepal
description: Youth-led NGO founded by Sudan Gurung, known for earthquake relief. Wikipedia reports it called the 8 September 2025 protest, used Discord and Instagram to coordinate, worked with about 140 influencers, and met army leadership after Oli's resignation.

title: The Himalayan Times
description: English-language daily founded 23 November 2001, owned by International Media Network Nepal. Wikipedia reports that the Press Council Nepal blacklisted it in 2025 after a complaint about its reporting, which the paper disputed.

title: Hotel Association Nepal
description: Trade body that reported hotel-sector losses from the September 2025 protests.

title: House of Representatives of Nepal
description: Lower house of the Federal Parliament, 275 seats. Dissolved on 12 September 2025; election held on 5 March 2026, in which the Rastriya Swatantra Party won 182 seats.

title: Human Rights Watch
description: International rights organisation. Its report of 19 November 2025 says researchers analysed and verified 50 videos from 8 September.

title: IBC24
description: Indian regional news channel. Decode reports it claimed Oli left a secret resignation letter.

title: India Today
description: Indian news group. BOOM names it among outlets that reported the death of Ravi Laxmi Chitrakar.

title: INSEC
description: Informal Sector Service Centre, a Nepali human rights organisation that runs INSEC Online, a human rights news portal; it published a statement condemning the use of force in the protests.

title: Instagram
description: Meta-owned platform. Named by the Kathmandu Post among the platforms that did not apply to register by the deadline and were blocked from 4 September 2025. Hami Nepal used its Instagram account to circulate protest information.

title: International Commission of Jurists (ICJ)
description: International jurists' organisation. Published and co-signed joint statements on 13 September 2025 and 12-13 February 2026.

title: Internet Service Providers Association of Nepal
description: Industry body that the NTA instructed to enforce the blocking, according to Swarajya.

title: Janata Samajwadi Party, Nepal
description: Founded 22 April 2020; chaired by Upendra Yadav. Won 12 of 275 seats in 2022. Several factions split from it between 2021 and 2025. Wikipedia's English title for the party is People's Socialist Party, Nepal (2020); a different party founded in 2024 by Ashok Rai uses a similar name.

title: Embassy of Japan in Kathmandu
description: Welcomed Karki's appointment as an important step in Nepal's transition, in a Facebook statement reported by The Himalayan Times via The Tribune.

title: Judicial inquiry commission on the 8-9 September 2025 events
description: Commission formed by the Karki cabinet on 21 September 2025 under the Commission of Inquiry Act, led by Gauri Bahadur Karki, with three months to report.

title: Kantipur Media Group
description: Publisher founded in 1993 (Kantipur Publications Pvt. Ltd.), chaired by Kailash Sirohiya; outlets include the Kantipur daily, The Kathmandu Post, Kantipur Television and Kantipur FM. During the Gen Z protests demonstrators forced staff from its headquarters and set fire to one building, per Wikipedia.

title: Kaski District Administration Office
description: Imposed an indefinite prohibitory order in Pokhara from 2 pm on 8 September 2025.

title: Kathmandu Central Jail
description: Prison in Dillibazar, Kathmandu, as located in OpenStreetMap; Wikipedia's account of the protests lists the Kathmandu main prison among the prisons where a breakout was reported thwarted.

title: Kathmandu District Court
description: District court that remanded Durga Prasai and an associate to 12 days of judicial custody on 11 April 2025.

title: Kathmandu District Security Committee
description: District committee that met on 7 September 2025 and concluded the overall security situation was normal, per Onlinekhabar.

title: Kathmandu Medical College Teaching Hospital
description: Hospital in Sinamangal named in reporting as having received dead or dying protesters on 8 September 2025.

title: Kathmandu Metropolitan City
description: Local government of Kathmandu; Balendra Shah was its mayor from 30 May 2022 to 18 January 2026, then Sunita Dangol acted as mayor (Wikipedia).

title: The Kathmandu Post
description: English-language daily founded in February 1993, owned by Kantipur Media Group; editor-in-chief Biswas Baral.

title: LinkedIn
description: Professional network. Named among the platforms that did not apply to register and were blocked from 4 September 2025.

title: Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock Development
description: Ministry headed by Ram Nath Adhikari until his resignation on 9 September 2025.

title: Ministry of Communication and Information Technology
description: Ministry whose directive led the Nepal Telecommunications Authority to publish a list of 26 platforms to be shut down in September 2025 (Kathmandu Post). Prithvi Subba Gurung was its minister from 15 July 2024 to 9 September 2025. Its website could not be fetched (certificate error).

title: Ministry of Defence
description: Located at Singha Durbar. Minister of Defence from 15 July 2024 to 9 September 2025 was Manbir Rai; its website lists the Prime Minister as also Defence Minister (accessed 2026-10-05).

title: Ministry of Education
description: Ministry led in the fourth Oli cabinet by CPN-UML's Bidya Bhattarai from 15 July 2024 to 21 April 2025.

title: Ministry of Education, Science and Technology
description: Ministry led by Mahabir Pun in the Karki interim cabinet, 22 September 2025 to 20 January 2026.

title: Ministry of Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation
description: Ministry held by Kulman Ghising from 15 September 2025 to 7 January 2026 (Karki interim cabinet).

title: Ministry of External Affairs (India)
description: Indian foreign ministry. Issued a statement on 9 September 2025 on developments in Nepal and an advisory to Indian nationals.

title: Ministry of Finance
description: Ministry headed in the Oli cabinet by Deputy Prime Minister Bishnu Prasad Paudel, in the Karki interim cabinet by Rameshwor Khanal and since 27 March 2026 by Swarnim Wagle.

title: Ministry of Foreign Affairs
description: Located at Singha Durbar, Kathmandu. Its website names Shisir Khanal as minister (accessed 2026-10-05).

title: Ministry of Foreign Affairs (China)
description: Chinese foreign ministry. Its spokesperson commented on Nepal on 10 September 2025.

title: Ministry of Health and Population
description: Ministry reported to have instructed hospitals to give free treatment to injured protesters on 8 September 2025.

title: Ministry of Home Affairs
description: Ministry that oversees Nepal Police and the Armed Police Force. Its website lists Sudhan (Sudan) Gurung as minister (accessed 2026-10-05).

title: Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs
description: Ministry held by Om Prakash Aryal from 15 to 22 September 2025, then by Anil Kumar Sinha.

title: Ministry of Urban Development
description: Ministry headed by Deputy Prime Minister Prakash Man Singh in the fourth Oli cabinet.

title: Ministry of Water Supply
description: Ministry headed by Pradip Yadav, who resigned on 9 September 2025.

title: Ministry of Youth and Sports
description: Ministry headed by Tejulal Chaudhary, who resigned on 9 September 2025.

title: Nakkhu Prison
description: Prison in Lalitpur established in 1950. Rabi Lamichhane was freed from Nakkhu prison on 9 September 2025 when protesters entered the facility (Wikipedia); he was later held there again until his bail on 19 December 2025 (Himal Press).

title: National Assembly of Nepal
description: Upper house of Nepal's federal parliament, where the Social Media Bill was introduced in early 2025.

title: National Council for Disaster Risk Reduction and Management
description: Council chaired by Prime Minister Balendra Shah. In early October 2026 it recommended a Rs559.17 billion budget for 504 reconstruction plans after the Bhotekoshi-Trishuli floods.

title: National Investigation Department
description: Nepal’s intelligence agency under the Prime Minister’s Office. Onlinekhabar reports it filed a six-point report on the Gen Z movement on 7 September 2025.

title: NDTV
description: Indian news broadcaster. Alt News and Decode report that NDTV channels aired old Pashupatinath Temple footage as an attack by protesters; BOOM lists NDTV among outlets that reported the death of Ravi Laxmi Chitrakar.

title: Nepal Bar Association
description: Lawyers' association founded in 1956 with headquarters on Ram Shah Path, Kathmandu.

title: Nepal Electricity Authority
description: State electricity utility; Kulman Ghising was its managing director from 2016 to 2020 and from 2021 until his removal on 24 March 2025 (Wikipedia).

title: Nepal Insurance Authority
description: Insurance regulator that reported claim totals from the September 2025 protest damage.

title: Nepal Police
description: National police force founded in 1955, under the Ministry of Home Affairs, headquartered at Naxal, Kathmandu, with 79,541 employees (Wikipedia). Inspector General: Chandra Kuber Khapung from 4 September 2025, then Dan Bahadur Karki.

title: Nepal Police Hospital
description: Hospital in Maharajgunj, Kathmandu, opened in 2040 BS (1983-84) for police personnel and families, now 400 beds and open to the public.

title: Nepal Telecommunications Authority
description: Autonomous telecom regulator established in 1998 under the Telecommunications Act 1997. Following the ministry's directive it published the list of 26 platforms to be shut down in September 2025 (Kathmandu Post, 5 September 2025).

title: Nepali Army
description: National army, headquartered at Jangi Adda, Bhadrakali, Kathmandu; Chief of the Army Staff is General Ashok Raj Sigdel (96,500 active personnel, 2026, Wikipedia).

title: Nepali Communist Party
description: Formed on 5 November 2025 by merging the CPN (Maoist Centre), CPN (Unified Socialist) and other communist groups, not CPN-UML. Coordinator Pushpa Kamal Dahal; co-coordinator Madhav Kumar Nepal; Jhalanath Khanal ranked third. Won 17 of 275 seats in 2026 (Wikipedia).

title: Nepali Congress
description: Party founded on 9 April 1950. Gagan Thapa has been president since January 2026, after Sher Bahadur Deuba's tenure that began in 2016. Won 89 seats in 2022 and 38 in 2026. Headquarters: B.P. Smriti Bhawan, Lalitpur (Wikipedia).

title: News18
description: Indian news broadcaster. Decode reports it framed the protest with a Hindu nation angle and carried a claim of a secret Oli resignation letter; BOOM lists it among outlets that reported the death of Ravi Laxmi Chitrakar.

title: National Human Rights Commission, Nepal
description: Constitutional human rights body chaired by Top Bahadur Magar since 3 February 2021. Its report on the protest killings, reported on 27 May 2026, held Oli primarily responsible and recommended action against Lekhak, Prithvi Subba Gurung and senior police officers.

title: Office of the President of Nepal
description: Office and official residence of the President of Nepal at Shital Niwas (Rashtrapati Bhavan), Maharajgunj. The Kathmandu Post calls Shital Niwas 'the President's office'.

title: Office of the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers
description: Executive office of the Government of Nepal at Singha Durbar, Kathmandu. Its website names Balendra Shah as Prime Minister (accessed 2026-10-05).

title: OHCHR
description: Office of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights, established 20 December 1993; Volker Türk has been High Commissioner since 17 October 2022.

title: World Organisation Against Torture (OMCT)
description: International network against torture. Co-signatory of the 9 September 2025 statement on the protest crackdown.

title: Online Khabar
description: Independent online news portal founded in 2006 with Nepali and English editions; founder and president Dharma Raj Bhusal.

title: Parliamentary special committee on cooperative fraud
description: Parliamentary special inquiry committee whose report concluded Rabi Lamichhane was involved in misuse of cooperative funds.

title: Pathao
description: Ride-hailing and delivery company. Its then managing director, Asheem Man Singh Basnyat, said he would join the 8 September 2025 protest at Maitighar.

title: Pinterest
description: Image-sharing platform. Named by the Guardian and Swarajya among the blocked platforms.

title: Pragatisheel Loktantrik Party
description: Party led by Baburam Bhattarai from 20 November 2025, formed in the split of the CPN (Maoist Centre) (Wikipedia pages on Bhattarai and the Maoist Centre).

title: High-level study committee on cases against Gen Z protesters
description: Committee headed by former High Court judge Baburam Regmi, with former Deputy Attorney General Chet Nath Ghimire and retired DIG Poshraj Pokharel. It submitted its report to Home Minister Sudan Gurung on 1 October 2026.

title: Rastriya Prajatantra Party
description: Founded 29 May 1990; chaired by Rajendra Lingden since December 2021. Won 14 seats in 2022 and 5 in 2026, losing national party status (Wikipedia).

title: Rastriya Swatantra Party
description: Founded 1 July 2022; chaired by Rabi Lamichhane. Won 21 seats in 2022 and 182 of 275 in the March 2026 election (47.84% of the proportional vote). Balen Shah leads the parliamentary party and became Prime Minister on 27 March 2026. Headquarters: Chamati, Kathmandu (Wikipedia).

title: Reddit
description: Forum platform founded 23 June 2005 in San Francisco. Reddit is on the Kathmandu Post list of the 26 platforms blocked on 4 September 2025.

title: Reporters Without Borders (RSF)
description: Press freedom organisation. Statements on the Social Media Bill (June 2025) and on media outlets and journalists attacked on 8 and 9 September 2025.

title: Republic TV
description: Indian news channel. Named by Newslaundry for saying the protest was a CIA plot, and by BOOM among outlets that reported the death of Ravi Laxmi Chitrakar.

title: Rupandehi District Administration Office
description: Imposed a curfew order in the Butwal-Bhairahawa area from 4 pm to 10 pm on 8 September 2025.

title: Committee to study security agencies' role on 8-9 September
description: Committee formed by the cabinet on 15 April 2026 under former High Court judge Prem Raj Karki, with former APF AIG Subodh Adhikari and former police AIG Tek Prasad Rai, to study the inquiry findings and security mechanisms.

title: Shram Sanskriti Party
description: Party founded by Harka Sampang, the former mayor of Dharan (Wikipedia).

title: sidhakura.com
description: News website whose publisher and executive editor were convicted of contempt by a Supreme Court extended full bench, the case in which the Court said online and social media platforms must register.

title: Signal
description: Messaging app. Named by the Guardian and Swarajya among the blocked platforms.

title: Special Task Force (Nepal Police)
description: Unit named as having fired from inside the Parliament compound on 8 September 2025. The Kathmandu Post names it only as the Special Task Force; Human Rights Watch calls it the Nepal Police's Special Task Force.

title: Sunsari District Administration Office
description: District administration of Sunsari, where Itahari is located. Reporting says a curfew was implemented in Itahari on 8 September 2025.

title: Supreme Court of Nepal
description: Apex court, a Chief Justice and twenty justices, seated on Ram Shah Path, Kathmandu. It declined to release Oli and Lekhak from detention (reported 31 March 2026).

title: Telegram
description: Messaging app by Telegram FZ-LLC, launched 2013. It does not appear in the Kathmandu Post list of the 26 platforms blocked on 4 September 2025; no source retrieved states its status in Nepal.

title: TikTok
description: Video app operated by ByteDance, launched 20 September 2016. The AP reported on 4 September 2025 that TikTok and Viber were allowed to keep operating in Nepal because they had registered with the government.

title: Times Now Navbharat
description: Indian Hindi-language news channel. Named by Newslaundry for a foreign-hand framing of the protests and by Decode for airing old Pashupatinath footage.

title: Times of India
description: Indian newspaper. BOOM names it among outlets that reported the death of Ravi Laxmi Chitrakar.

title: National Trauma Centre, Kathmandu
description: Trauma hospital on Mahankal Marg, Kathmandu, as located in OpenStreetMap. No other source was retrieved for its description.

title: Tribhuvan University
description: Nepal's oldest university, founded 25 June 1959; main campus at Kirtipur.

title: Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital
description: Teaching hospital on Maharajgunj Road, Kathmandu, founded in 1982.

title: Tribhuvan University Institute of Medicine, forensic medicine department
description: Department that carried out postmortem examinations of protest victims, according to Reuters (26 September 2025).

title: Tulsipur High Court
description: High court whose Butwal bench ordered Rabi Lamichhane's release on bail on 18 December 2025.

title: Ujyaalo Nepal Party
description: Party whose chairman from 10 January 2026 is Kulman Ghising (Wikipedia).

title: UN Nepal
description: United Nations country presence in Nepal; its information platform at un.org.np carries UN humanitarian coordination, cluster and resource pages (accessed 2026-10-05).

title: United Nations
description: Intergovernmental organisation. Its Secretary-General's spokesperson, the High Commissioner for Human Rights, OHCHR spokesperson and the Resident Coordinator in Nepal each commented on the September 2025 events.

title: United States Department of State
description: US foreign ministry. Lowered its travel advisory for Nepal to Level 2 after the demonstrations ended.

title: Embassy of the United States in Kathmandu
description: US diplomatic mission. Signed the joint statement of 9 September 2025 and issued a shelter-in-place advisory to US citizens.

title: Viber
description: Messaging platform. Listed as registered with the ministry, so not blocked on 4 September 2025.

title: WhatsApp
description: Meta-owned messaging platform. Named among the platforms that did not apply to register and were blocked from 4 September 2025.

title: WION
description: Indian English-language news channel. Alt News says a WION journalist posted the claim that Oli never visited India as prime minister.

title: X (formerly Twitter)
description: Social network launched 15 July 2006, renamed X on 23 July 2023. X was among the 26 platforms blocked in Nepal in September 2025; the Kathmandu Post headline says X responded to the registration call.

title: Youth Against Corruption
description: Discord channel named in Wikipedia's account of the 2025 protests as one of the online groups.

title: YouTube
description: Video platform launched 23 April 2005, owned by Google/Alphabet. Blocked in Nepal on 4 September 2025 (AP).

title: Zee News
description: Indian television news channel. AFP reported that an anchor said rioters hiding in the Gen Z protest crowd tried to vandalise Pashupatinath Temple.
